# A1: pqcrypto 1.0.0 ML-DSA-44 signing (generated by bench/bench_primitives.py)

Single process, pinned core, 500 iterations each, 200-B message unless noted. Times in microseconds.

| variant | median | p10 | p90 | p99 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| flat sign(sk,msg) pure, no context | 6311.9 | 6202.1 | 7577.8 | 10135.4 |
| flat sign, context='EMBER-root' | 6245.4 | 6193.7 | 7148.9 | 11957.2 |
| object API SecretKey(sk).sign | 6333.4 | 6202.7 | 7103.3 | 11986.9 |
| HashML-DSA pre-hash SHA-256 | 6376.6 | 6208.6 | 7609.8 | 11741.5 |
| flat sign, 32-B message | 6383.4 | 6233.7 | 7100.1 | 9385.0 |
| verify (reference) | 119.9 | 113.5 | 135.2 | 552.8 |
| keygen (reference) | 140.4 | 127.9 | 153.7 | 195.8 |

Backend source files compiled into pqcrypto.abi3.so (from `strings`): backbone-ml-dsa-0.2.0/src/backends/soft.rs

sign/verify ratio (pqcrypto): 52.6x; sign/keygen: 45.0x.
OpenSSL 3.5.4 native (native_sig_agg.csv): keygen 91.8, sign 408.8, verify 100.9 us; sign/verify 4.0x.
pqcrypto/native: keygen 1.5x, sign 15.4x, verify 1.2x.

Max relative difference among the sign variants: 1.1%.

Interpretation: The API path, context string, message length and pre-hash mode do not explain the slowdown (variants within 1%). The binding is a Rust crate (backbone-ml-dsa) compiled with a portable `soft` backend (no AVX2); signing runs the rejection loop (expected ~4.25 iterations for ML-DSA-44), each NTT-heavy, so a slow portable NTT inflates sign much more than verify. All issuer-side (sign) claims in the paper therefore use the OpenSSL 3.5.4 native numbers; pqcrypto sign times are never presented as 'ML-DSA signing cost'.
